questions.q: How is Azure Policy fundamentally different from RBAC?
options: RBAC controls who can do what; Policy controls what's allowed to exist at all, regardless of who's creating it
They are two names for the exact same system
Policy only applies to billing, RBAC only applies to security
RBAC controls what's allowed to exist; Policy controls who can act
questions.explain: Policy can block a non-compliant deployment even for someone with full Contributor rights — it's a separate layer from permissions.

questions.q: What is the difference between a policy's "deny" effect and its "audit" effect?
options: Deny blocks a non-compliant deployment outright; audit just flags the violation without blocking it
Deny and audit do exactly the same thing
Audit blocks deployments; deny only sends an email
Deny only applies to tags, audit only applies to regions
questions.explain: Audit is useful while you're still figuring out what your rules should be, before committing to blocking deployments.

questions.q: What is a tag, and what does it actually change about a resource?
options: A name/value pair attached to a resource — it doesn't change how the resource works, only how you can find, group, and bill it later
A setting that changes the resource's performance tier
A security credential required to access the resource
A billing discount applied automatically to reserved instances
questions.explain: Tags like CostCenter: Marketing implement the "accountability" principle from Cost Management by making costs filterable by team, project, or environment.

questions.q: What does a management group let an organization do?
options: Apply RBAC and Policy once at a level above subscriptions, so it's inherited by every subscription underneath
Replace resource groups entirely
Bill multiple subscriptions as if they were a single VM
Tag resources automatically without any manual input
questions.explain: Management groups add one more layer above subscriptions: management groups -> subscriptions -> resource groups -> resources.

questions.q: Why would a large company apply a "no resources outside East US" policy at the management group level instead of subscription by subscription?
options: So every subscription beneath that management group inherits the rule automatically, without configuring it separately for each one
Because policies can only be applied at the management group level, never at a subscription
Because management groups are cheaper to use than subscriptions
Because RBAC requires it to be set at that level
questions.explain: Applying broad rules once, at the top of the hierarchy, avoids repeating the same configuration across every subscription.
